title: Sustainability progress is becoming a commercial and resilience capability, but policy, geopolitical, and financing divergence shapes who moves fastest
source_unit: World Economic Forum, Chief Sustainability Officers' Outlook September 2026
geography: Global sustainability transition perspectives from 103 chief sustainability officers across five continents

denominator.unit: anonymized chief sustainability officer responses from the WEF global CSO Community

progress_stable_or_accelerate.unit: percent expecting global sustainability progress to remain stable or accelerate over the next year

company_investment_stable_or_accelerate.unit: approximately three-quarters expecting company transition-related investment to remain unchanged or accelerate

geopolitical_drag.unit: percent expecting geopolitical and macroeconomic conditions to drag on sustainability progress

compliance_lens.value: roughly two-thirds say C-suite leaders still view sustainability primarily through a compliance lens

observations.method: WEF targeted survey of 103 CSO Community members, consultations, and open-text input; questions were framed globally and not disaggregated by region.
observations.uncertainty: This is a purposive executive sample, not a representative business or economy survey; leadership expectations may differ from implemented spending, emissions, adaptation, or worker and consumer outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Chief sustainability officers and large-company sustainability leaders across five continents, with company and sector perspectives represented unevenly.
observations.counterinterpretation: Executive confidence can reflect organizational strategy, signaling, or selection into the CSO community; stable investment expectations do not establish environmental progress or inclusive benefits.

observations.period: 2026; medium-term drivers and constraints on sustainability progress

business_case_accelerator.unit: percent selecting a stronger business case for sustainability measures as a leading three-year accelerator

technology_cost_accelerator.unit: percent selecting lower costs and greater availability of sustainable technologies

policy_uncertainty_constraint.unit: percent selecting policy reversals or inconsistent regulatory signals as a leading constraint

short_term_pressure_constraint.unit: percent selecting business short-term performance pressures as a leading constraint

international_agreements_driver.unit: percent selecting international agreements as a leading three-year driver

observations.method: WEF CSO survey asking respondents to select up to three accelerators and constraints for sustainability progress over the next three years.
observations.uncertainty: Selections describe executive expectations and priorities, not the relative causal power of business cases, technology, policy, or agreements; responses can reflect current corporate incentives and geopolitical context.
observations.subgroup: CSOs assessing corporate strategy, regulation, technology costs, capital allocation, and multilateral coordination.
observations.counterinterpretation: Commercial framing can accelerate deployment, but policy and international coordination may remain necessary to address externalities, distribution, standards, and collective-action problems.

observations.period: 2026; AI as sustainability accelerator and resource trade-off

ai_sustainability_accelerator.unit: percent expecting AI and other digital technologies to support sustainability progress over the next year

ai_infrastructure_negative_impact.unit: percent identifying AI infrastructure's energy and resource intensity as its most significant negative impact

ai_use_route.value: risk modelling, process and resource efficiency, measurement, and reporting

green_economy_scale.value: WEF estimates the green economy exceeded $5 trillion in annual value in 2024 and could exceed $7 trillion by 2030

observations.method: WEF CSO survey and report synthesis on AI's operational role, infrastructure footprint, and sustainability-related business activity.
observations.uncertainty: Expected acceleration is not measured emissions reduction, verified resource efficiency, or net environmental benefit; green-economy estimates and AI effects use different scopes and assumptions.
observations.subgroup: Companies deploying AI, sustainability teams, data-centre and technology providers, energy systems, and organizations measuring climate and nature risks.
observations.counterinterpretation: AI may improve measurement and efficiency while increasing electricity, water, hardware, and supply-chain burdens; net effects depend on deployment, energy mix, rebound, and governance.

observations.period: 2026; adaptation, resilience investment, and green divergence

adaptation_priority.unit: percent expecting adaptation to become a greater global focus over the next three years

private_investment_decisive.unit: percent agreeing private-sector investment will be decisive to scaling adaptation

uncertain_cost_benefit.unit: percent citing uncertain cost-benefit assessments as a key constraint on adaptation investment

emerging_market_leadership.value: around two-thirds expect emerging markets to play a growing leadership role

uneven_commercial_gains.value: over three-quarters expect commercial gains from sustainability to be uneven across sectors and markets

observations.method: WEF CSO survey on adaptation priority, investment, cost-benefit assessment, emerging-market leadership, and distribution of commercial gains.
observations.uncertainty: Expectations do not establish adaptation investment, avoided losses, resilience, or equitable distribution; cost-benefit uncertainty may reflect measurement gaps, discounting, financing, or policy risk.
observations.subgroup: Companies, infrastructure and supply-chain operators, emerging markets, investors, insurers, and communities exposed to climate and nature risks.
observations.counterinterpretation: Uneven pathways can support locally appropriate innovation and leadership; commercial divergence can also widen protection gaps where capital, grids, insurance, and public capacity are weak.

related_sources.claim: WEF Chief Economists' Outlook provides complementary macroeconomic, AI investment, cost-of-living, and geopolitical context.
IEA World Energy Investment provides complementary energy-investment and transition-capital context.
WEF Global Risks Report provides complementary climate, geopolitical, technological, and societal risk context.

boundary: This record adds a corporate sustainability and adaptation route across business value, policy uncertainty, geopolitics, AI resource trade-offs, climate adaptation, resilience finance, emerging-market leadership, and uneven transition gains. It uses a targeted CSO survey and executive synthesis, not representative corporate behavior, verified emissions or adaptation outcomes, community consent, causal investment effects, or proof that green growth is inclusive.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official WEF Chief Sustainability Officers' Outlook September 2026 page and linked PDF were retrieved and reviewed for sample frame, progress outlook, business-case and policy drivers, AI trade-offs, adaptation investment, and green-divergence claims.
